historical_prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE high resolution landscape art direction contact sheet for the first-person business game HUSTLE & SCALE. Title 'A / Grounded Realism'. Original concept illustration, not real engine screenshot. Photoreal grounded contemporary working-class urban realism. Full realistic human anatomy and faces, complex believable scuffed metal and rubber, ambient daylight through grimy glazing, physically detailed plaster and concrete, utilitarian grey UI with fine white type, realistic municipal retail architecture. No cinematic fog. Matter-of-fact industrial photography.
Exactly same scenario for comparison: small rented urban workshop, one long bench facing a courtyard doorway, wooden crate holding THREE identical square rechargeable WORK LIGHTS, tabletop diagnostic meter, one adult local buyer at doorway. This is legal used-equipment trading, no crime paraphernalia.
Editorial art-board composition with hierarchy, generous readable images: top half one wide first-person GAMEPLAY CONCEPT at human eye height viewing the workbench; bottom half four useful visual samples: (1) closeup of ONE square worklight front/side and battery cover (2) full adult NPC (3) compact inventory strip with three physical-unit slots (4) purchase docket showing 3 × work lights / $180 / $300 → $120. A small 5-swatch palette strip and type specimen, with material details in images. Show ordinary courtyard location through open doorway and workstation in gameplay image. UI minimal and deliberately matching this art direction, legible, no standard rounded dashboard cards. All three units look same model with different cosmetic wear; no red light or label revealing hidden battery fault before test. Product foot about 29cm wide, housing about 24cm wide; avoid huge handheld searchlights. No extra goods or invented economy. Use labels in concise English to avoid illegible text. Emphasize visual execution and differences of shape, surface, lighting, character and interface, not just colors. Only concept/art direction samples.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create a single plain unpolished FIRST-PERSON VIDEO GAME SCREENSHOT CONCEPT for Hustle & Scale. Use the ATTACHED SEARCH-SCREENSHOT GRID as the VISUAL REFERENCE: study the actual in-game Schedule I screenshots in its tiles, particularly the thin lanky NPCs in yellow/green shirts, the simple warehouse tables and square store interiors. Match that level of 3D simplification and ordinary indie Unity game rendering. This is NOT a collage of the reference, NOT concept painting, NOT high-end animation, NOT realistic, NOT Pixar, NOT Disney, NOT cozy diorama, NOT polished toy product advertising.
Scene: human eye height inside a small undecorated rented workshop with offwhite flat plaster walls and grey concrete floor. A plain straight rectangular plywood bench on square grey steel legs, three identical portable square blue rechargeable WORK LIGHTS about 30cm each, black rectangular top grips, simple recessed pale lens, flat rubber feet, wooden three-slot transport crate to the left. Each lamp is no more than a few broad geometric parts, no detailed LED arrays or screw patterns. Small simple test meter at right. Large empty usable area on worktop. Metal shelf with a few brown boxes. Ordinary open rectangular door to small urban yard of simple rectangular buildings, straight fence, plain sidewalk and old low-poly utility van. Slightly imperfect practical arrangement, no artfully styled decorative clutter.
ONE male adult NPC standing by doorway, with tall slim body, long thin arms and legs, very plain muted green short-sleeve shirt and straight navy trousers. Elongated oval head, simple eyes with whites and dots, narrow simple mouth, basic block hair, subtle mildly tired neutral expression. Small simple nose, no big bulbous nose, no huge cheeks, no friendly cartoon grin, no meticulously sculpted face, no plush smoothness. Do not make a beautiful animated-movie character. Render body and clothing as straightforward low-detail meshes with smooth plain color, like actual modest-budget game NPCs in reference. Low polygon count but no decorative faceting.
Lighting is ordinary daytime Unity rasterized rendering: one sun, soft ambient room lighting, readable modest shadows, ordinary camera with vertical FOV about 70. Matte diffuse surfaces with restrained broad material difference, simple texture only. No dramatic cinematic lighting, no volumetric beams, no bloom, no depth of field, no bevels on everything, no fancy film grading. Broad slate blue equipment, pale walls, ordinary brown wood, grey metal, small muted ochre price label. Small unobtrusive HUD top left '$120', bottom 3 square inventory slots, centered small 'E — Inspect'. Keep text minimal. Wide 16:9 framing. Primary goal: a believable ACTUAL SIMPLE 3D GAME frame, almost like a screenshot from an indie simulator using simple models, not aspirational concept art. Label tiny 'HUSTLE & SCALE / CONCEPT' at lower left.

Create an original art direction comparison sheet C / DISTRICT INK for Hustle & Scale. Use attached plain indie-game workshop concept as content reference, keep its level of simple game geometry but DIFFERENT rendering language: very restrained comic-ink 3D, 2-tone hard cel shadows, thin navy contour only on silhouettes, no halftone noise on objects, flat brick paint and buff plaster, compressed street architecture with tall narrow storefronts. Plain lanky adult NPC with oval head and thin arms, graphic short straight hair, simple eyes and narrow mouth, no exaggerated Disney nose or smile. Same situation: first-person small rented workshop, long square plywood bench, THREE square rechargeable worklights in wooden crate, meter on bench, local buyer at ordinary open doorway. Top 65% wide gameplay concept; bottom strip closeup one lamp, full-body NPC, square 3-slot inventory, narrow purchase slip exactly '3 LAMPS / $180 / $300 > $120', swatches navy, brick red, cream, ochre, grey. Sharp square UI, poster-influenced sans typography. NO realism, no photographic metal/wood, no cinematic glow, no diorama, no toy roundness. Simple game render, deliberately sparse utilitarian life. Label CONCEPT.

Create an original art direction comparison sheet D / FIELD MANUAL for Hustle & Scale. Attached workshop concept is content reference. This direction uses an ENTIRELY DIFFERENT FORM LANGUAGE: square slab construction, thin rectilinear steel frames, chamfered shallow planes like robust industrial assembly, long horizontal signs, restrained engraved seam lines; cool grey body surfaces with cobalt functional parts and buff paper. Simplified industrial handbook-like 3D with clean flat shaded planes and very few textures, consistent parallel bevel edges, no black comic outlines. World is full-scale first-person playable geometry, not cardboard, miniature diorama, isometric or blueprint. NPC thin adult, narrow rectangular torso, elongated plain head, simple small eyes and short mouth, angular slab hair, practical jacket, no Pixar face. Same scenario: small rented workshop, straight long bench and THREE square rechargeable worklights in crate, simple meter, buyer at open doorway. Top 65% gameplay concept in ordinary daylight; bottom strip one lamp front/side/back, NPC, numbered 3-slot inventory, purchase slip exactly '3 LAMPS / $180 / $300 > $120', 5 swatches. UI like printed technical tab indexes and square ivory receipt, strictly simple sans type. NO photorealism, no cinematic render, no beautiful cozy illustration, no excessive graphic overlays. It should look like an actually producible simple indie 3D game. Label CONCEPT.

Create a production-oriented asset concept sheet for HUSTLE & SCALE using the ATTACHED IMAGE AS THE STRONG STYLE TARGET. Precisely retain its plain modest-budget Unity game appearance, simple utilitarian geometry and lanky neutral NPC. Do not prettify into Disney/Pixar/cozy diorama or photorealism. Landscape sheet with four useful zones: (1) front, side and back views of same blue square rechargeable worklight with black rectangular top handle, foot 29cm wide and housing24cm; extremely simple broad geometry, plain lens, minimal screws; (2) broad material chips steel, painted blue metal, graphite rubber, offwhite lens, plywood, cardboard, paper, textile, clear glass, plaster with no noisy detail; (3) adult slim NPC neutral front side back, green T-shirt/navy trousers, elongated oval head, very simple eyes and flat mouth, thin arms, two alternate workwear silhouettes sharing body, NO cute nose cheeks grin; (4) worklight states unknown / tested working / tested battery fault / repaired requires retest, same external shell all states, mark fault only with meter and removable paper tag after test, not red glowing housing. No text beyond short labels. Objects should read like basic meshes in ordinary realtime 3D game viewport, not manufactured luxury products. Quiet neutral backdrop, functional organization.

Create a paired environment concept sheet for HUSTLE & SCALE in exactly the ATTACHED plain modest-budget Unity first-person game style. NO photorealism, NO Disney/Pixar, no rounded toy props, no cozy diorama, no cinematic advertising. Simple game geometry, matte flat materials, plain functional architecture. TWO EQUAL wide panels same eye-height camera angle and same room footprint, a plain small rented working room with door to yard. Left EARLY: one straight plywood bench on steel legs, plain meter, one wooden crate for 3 simple square blue rechargeable worklights, sparsely stocked shelf, hand-lettered physical labels, usable empty floor and bench space. Right ORGANIZED FUTURE: same bench and room, one added simple shelving bay, structured three storage bins, clearer printed location labels, consistent packing boxes and one neutral worklight over bench, slightly better organized worktop, same modest level of simple geometry. Progress conveyed by organization and process, not magical expensive mansion, glossy furniture, more bloom or automatic upgrade after first sale. Small lower strip shows unpacked lamp, paper protective sleeve, finished box with simple single-corner-cut label and imaginary small manufacturer mark VERTA. Keep commodity model and scale the same. Label CONCEPT / FUTURE ORGANIZATION STUDY. No prices or invented upgrade unlocks.

Edit only the bottom-right REPAIRED REQUIRES RETEST worklight panel: replace the green tick/checkmark on its hanging tag with a dark graphite QUESTION MARK. The repaired unit requires retesting, so it MUST NOT display verified green success. Keep all other images, proportions, text, panels, layout and rendering unchanged. Preserve title REPAIRED REQUIRES RETEST. This is a precise correction to a game art sheet.

current_edits.prompt: Edit ONLY the adult NPC at the doorway. Keep the SAME simple indie 3D simulator visual style and degree of stylization as this image, visually comparable to Schedule I gameplay: plain low-detail meshes, thin adult limbs, simplified eyes and mouth, ordinary realtime game lighting. Do NOT invent a new art style and do NOT make it realistic, Disney, Pixar or cute. Make the character an original local tradesman rather than a duplicate of a Schedule I NPC: subtly angular longer jaw, moderately half-lidded simple eyes with visible whites but not spherical protruding eyeballs, one eyebrow slightly uneven, short dark swept-back hair with a modest receding corner, plain dark indigo open work overshirt over light grey T-shirt, straight dark trousers. Neutral practical expression, no smile. Retain thin simple adult body and basic game-model appearance. Preserve all workshop geometry, lighting, framing, lamps, crate, meter, background, UI, text and colors exactly. This is an original character in the SAME visual style, not a departure from it.

Preserve ALL upper-left lamp views, upper-right material chips, and lower-right interaction states, text, numbers, layout and lighting exactly. Especially preserve question-mark tag for REPAIRED REQUIRES RETEST and red fault tag. Do not alter or add any game rules.
